_note: Curated map from a work to the primary text that can actually be read for it.
Editorial data, not derived: correct it by hand when a source is identified or
ruled out. Every entry states how it was verified, so nothing here is trusted
on the strength of a filename alone.
Paths are relative to the project root and point into database/extracted_markdown/,
which is git-ignored and regenerable. No primary text is stored in this file.

_status_values.ready: full text located and structurally split; safe to read from
_status_values.needs_structure: full text located, but chapter boundaries are not yet reliable
_status_values.unresolved: text is present in a container file whose boundaries are not yet found
_status_values.no_primary_text: no readable primary text in the corpus; dossier must rely on criticism and PKD's own commentary

novels.title: Ubik
novels.verified: 21 h2 headings, of the form 'Chapter N'; word count consistent with the novel

novels.title: A Maze of Death
novels.verified: the pattern finds only 12 of the novel's 16 chapters: headings for chapters 6, 8, 11 and 13 were dropped by the PDF conversion, so each is currently fused into the chapter before it. Six further headings ('MADE AT TERRA 35082R', 'WINERY', 'STOPPERY', 'WITCHERY', 'HIPPERY HOPPERY', 'MEKKISRY') are in-world text promoted to headings, not chapter markers.

novels.title: The Game-Players of Titan
novels.verified: 15 h2 headings, but at least one is a fragment of prose ('understand.') promoted by the PDF conversion; the numeric headings need checking before chapter spans are trusted

novels.title: The Man in the High Castle
novels.verified: full text present and clean, but the file carries no headings at all; chapter boundaries must be recovered from the text itself

novels.title: The Transmigration of Timothy Archer

novels.title: A Scanner Darkly
novels.verified: DOC_ARCH_SCANNERDARKLY.md is NOT the novel. It runs to 28,129 words and contains 135 INT./EXT. slug lines, so it is a screenplay adaptation. Reading it as the novel would misattribute screenplay material to Dick's prose.
